summary: Added the missing dropdown indicator to the header nav, renamed the About O360 top-level item to Company, gave it About O360 and Products children, and rebuilt /products/ as the full products-and-services catalogue (un-retired: republished to the index and its blanket redirect switched off).

1_header_nav_dropdown_indicator.finding: The widget carried indicator:"none" AND submenu_icon:{"value":"","library":""}. In Elementor Pro 4.2.1 the 'indicator' select control no longer exists in nav-menu.php at all — it is dead legacy data. The control that actually renders is submenu_icon (an ICONS control) whose default is fas fa-caret-down. The explicit empty value was overriding that default, so the four dropdown parents had no caret, chevron or any other affordance that a submenu existed.

changed.why: chevron-down is the only indicator Elementor's own stylesheet down-sizes automatically (.sub-arrow .fas.fa-chevron-down{font-size:.7em}), so it costs the least width in a 0.7em uppercase menu.

Elementor Pro ships .elementor-nav-menu .sub-arrow{padding:10px;padding-inline-end:0}. 10px of lead-in per parent item is too much for this menu. 4px keeps the bar from growing. Scoped to --main so the mobile dropdown keeps the roomier default. Spacing only — no colour, no font — so the global-styles rule is not touched.

1_header_nav_dropdown_indicator.indicator_key_left_in_place: The legacy indicator:"none" key was NOT removed. It is not read by Elementor Pro 4.2.1, and deleting it is churn with no effect.
1_header_nav_dropdown_indicator.verified: post-86551.css regenerated (19,373 bytes) and contains the custom rule. Rendering template 86551 server-side produces <span class="sub-arrow"> on exactly the 4 parents with children — Web Design, Marketing, SEO/PPC, Company — as inline SVG (the e_font_icon_svg experiment is active and fas/chevron-down resolves from solid.json).

6_products_page_rebuilt.layout_method: The /websites/ hub (86671) was used as the literal source. Its container settings (b377238), 50% column (33d151a), inner row (b9b1f01), sub-column (82ca4e1), group heading (4087061), icon-list (c5a6c28) and header section (d72ff19 / 6155b4a / d66207e / 940fcaa) were cloned, so background colour, the pattern-organic overlay at 0.54 opacity with multiply blend, the 1400px boxed width, icon size 19, text indent 18 and 12px item spacing all carry across exactly. For the Web Design group the entire DENTAL+HEALTH and MEDICAL column subtrees were cloned rather than rebuilt, so all 47 specialty links keep their original labels, icons and order.
6_products_page_rebuilt.id_safety: Every cloned node was re-IDed against the union of all element IDs on both pages. The result was checked for duplicates before saving — 143 unique IDs, zero collisions.

6_products_page_rebuilt.one_deliberate_deviation_from_the_source: On /websites/ the DENTAL / HEALTH / MEDICAL headings are h2. Here they are h4, because on this page they sit underneath an h3 product heading which sits underneath the h2 catalogue header. The global typography on them is unchanged (still 'Widget Title (h3)') — only the HTML tag differs, which CLAUDE.md rule 6 explicitly allows: choose the global style by its name, not by its tag. Final outline: h1 hero -> h2 catalogue header -> h3 product -> h4 sub-group.

icons.mechanism: Font Awesome Pro is loaded as a kit (option elementor_font_awesome_pro_kit_id). Elementor's e_font_icon_svg experiment is active, but its SVG map only covers Free (solid/regular/brands json), so 'fal' icons fall through to <i class="fal fa-x"> and are swapped client-side by the kit. Verified identical markup on /websites/ and on the new sections.
icons.caveat: The nine new names are standard Font Awesome Pro Light icons, but the kit is resolved in the browser so this could not be confirmed server-side. Worth one look at the live page.

note_on_page_caching.finding: Code snippet #13 'Pagely Compatibility - Disable WP Rocket Page Caching' is active and returns false for do_rocket_generate_caching_files. WP Rocket is therefore NOT the page-HTML cache on this site — Pagely's edge cache is.
note_on_page_caching.consequence: The header change (chevron + Company rename) affects every page on the site, and nothing that can be done from this connector purges Pagely. Pages will show the new header as their edge cache expires, or immediately after a Pagely purge from the host panel.
note_on_page_caching.why_it_matters: rocket_clean_post() calls in this and previous batches still do useful work on the used-CSS / above-the-fold / lazy-render tables, but they were never the thing serving cached HTML.
